# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-25
**Member:** Emerson Delgado
**Member ID:** W249568388
**Reference number:** POC-926BF4D7E4-25977
**Requested service:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Ordering surgeon:** Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Plan:** Simply Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), State of Florida
**Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML) — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval. The notice dated 2026-08-25 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. I believe the records already in my file address the plan's own published criteria, and in this letter I map each criterion to the specific documentation.

I am citing the Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 guideline above. The quoted language below is taken word for word from that guideline. Anything outside quotation marks is my own description of my records.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The pathway that applies to me.** The guideline describes a category of tear that begins with:

> "Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months"

My records describe exactly that: 18 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest, with no traumatic injury reported. The guideline's separate acute pathway requires "Traumatic injury within the preceding 3 months with no preexisting shoulder pain (For traumatic injuries that occurred more than 3 months ago, see chronic or degenerative full thickness tear )," which is not my situation and should not be the standard applied to my request.

**2. Duration of symptoms.** The guideline requires:

> "Symptoms are present for at least 3 months"

My documented symptom duration is 18 months of progressive pain.

**3. Imaging.** The guideline requires:

> "Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a degenerative full thickness tear"

and, as to documentation:

> "Imaging report . The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

I had an MRI of the shoulder on 2026-06-18. It reports a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. That study was obtained within the past 12 months and is a detailed report identifying the tear, its thickness, its size and the degree of fatty atrophy. If this report was not matched to my file during the review, I ask that it be located and read before a decision is made on this appeal; if it is missing, please tell me in writing so my surgeon's office can resend it.

**4. Conservative management.** The guideline requires:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

and defines what that care must contain:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records document supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics from 2026-05-10 to 2026-07-05 — 8 weeks, with 16 visits completed. That is physical therapy, and it exceeds six weeks. Alongside it, I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. That is physical therapy plus more than one additional conservative treatment, and none of it resolved my symptoms.

**5. Proof that I completed and complied with that care.** The guideline requires:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

and:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, which records 16 completed visits across the full course of therapy. A discharge note is the record of a completed course, not an abandoned one.

**6. Pain and function.** The guideline refers to:

> "Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living"

My records document pain that is unrelieved by rest, that has progressed over 18 months, and that limits my daily life in concrete ways: I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. I want to be accurate with the plan — the summary I have does not contain a numeric VAS score. If a numbered score is the specific item the plan found missing, please say so in writing and I will ask Dr. Duval's office to supply it promptly, rather than have my request denied for a single data point that was never requested.

**7. Examination findings.** The guideline refers to:

> "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic rotator cuff tear (e.g., drop arm test, painful arc, full/empty can test, weakness of internal/external rotation or abduction)"

My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**8. Tobacco.** The guideline states:

> "For primary rotator cuff repair, adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco and nicotine products for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended."

I am a non-smoker. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## Please identify the criteria that were actually applied

The denial notice says my documentation was incomplete, but it does not tell me which specific item was found to be missing. I also want to be transparent about a limit on what I can see: one of the guideline passages I have — "Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for an acute full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met:" — ends in a colon and introduces a list of further conditions that was not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. I am not going to guess at what that list says.

Because the plan holds the criteria it applied, I am asking the plan to provide me, in writing and free of charge, the complete clinical review criteria used to deny CPT 29827 in my case, including the full text of each criterion and the specific criterion or document the reviewer found unmet. My plan uses Carelon for musculoskeletal surgery, and Carelon publishes its guidelines publicly with no login, so the applicable Joint Surgery guideline is readily available to the reviewer. I am asking for the version and sections actually applied to my request.

## What I am asking for

I ask that this denial be overturned and that the rotator cuff repair requested by Dr. Duval be authorized. In the alternative, if any single document or data point is genuinely missing from my file, I ask that the plan identify it in writing so it can be supplied, rather than let an incomplete-documentation finding stand when the MRI report, the physical therapy discharge note, the injection and medication history, and the examination findings are all part of my record.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-21, which is within 180 days of the 2026-08-25 notice. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to file can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Please send your written determination to me at the address below. I would also like to be told what further levels of review, including external review, remain available to me if this appeal is not decided in my favor.

Thank you for your time and for taking a careful second look at my records.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Delgado**
